questions.q: What does GROUP BY GROUPING SETS let you do that ROLLUP and CUBE don't?
options: Specify an exact, custom list of subtotal combinations instead of a fixed hierarchy or the full power set
Group on more than 32 columns at once
Aggregate without using any aggregate functions
Skip the GROUP BY clause entirely
questions.explain: ROLLUP always produces a fixed hierarchy and CUBE always produces every combination; GROUPING SETS returns only the exact combinations you list.

questions.q: What does an empty pair of parentheses, (), represent inside a GROUPING SETS list?
options: The grand total row — a grouping set with no grouping columns at all
A row with every column set to NULL on purpose, unrelated to totals
The same thing as ROLLUP's first row
questions.explain: An empty grouping set () produces exactly one row: the grand total across the whole result, with no grouping columns applied.

questions.q: Which GROUPING SETS list is equivalent to GROUP BY ROLLUP (Color, Size)?
questions.explain: ROLLUP (Color, Size) rolls up right to left: full detail, a Color subtotal, then the grand total — exactly those three grouping sets.

questions.q: Which GROUPING SETS list is equivalent to GROUP BY CUBE (Color, Size)?
questions.explain: CUBE produces every possible combination of the two columns — all four grouping sets, including a Size-alone subtotal ROLLUP never produces.

questions.q: You want only a Color+Size detail row and a grand total — no Color-alone subtotal. Which is correct?
questions.explain: Listing only (Color, Size) and () gives exactly the detail rows plus a grand total — neither ROLLUP nor CUBE can skip the Color subtotal this way.
